roadmap.title: Step 1 — Story, Chapters 1–2 (about 30 hours of the 60–80 hour story)
roadmap.body: Play the story and enjoy it. Do the Chapter 1 balcony meditation for Positive Mental Attitude the morning after Down to Earth — it is the only thing in the game that can lock. Scan every new vehicle with the WAiNK app and study new animals through the binoculars as you meet them; the 100% checklist later wants 200 of 277 vehicles and 100 of 255 animals. Keep a manual save at the start and end of each chapter (15 slots; missions cannot be replayed).

roadmap.title: Step 2 — Story, Chapters 3–5 and the finale
roadmap.body: Finish the story. The remaining chapter and mission trophies pop as the chapters close, and the final mission pops the gold You Gotta Know When to Get Off. Play the stranger strands as they appear — Andy is Lucia-only, Tyrone and Bret are Jason-only. Save before the final mission.

roadmap.title: Step 3 — Side stories, activities and robberies
roadmap.body: Finish the 8 stranger strands, the shooting-range golds (42), the drone races (14 locations), 20 different race wins, the 5 bank vaults and one illegal operation per gang (9). Robberies feed Marked Bills for Dime on the Dollar and the money for the 8 garages.

roadmap.title: Step 4 — Collectibles and the 100% checklist (about 100 hours)
roadmap.body: After the credits, open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion and work the checklist: 70 of 80 challenges, 15 card sets, 100 WAiNK locations, 33 underwater discoveries, 100 flamingos, 250 stunts (300 for 100%), 18 meditations (15 for 100%). A Long Road pops when the checklist hits 100% — PowerPyx calls it the hardest trophy, on time alone — and the platinum follows.

disputes: Grade split: one guide (Push Square, via GTAViceCityHub) lists 5 silver / 47 bronze where PowerPyx and Insider Gaming list 6 silver / 46 bronze. This guide follows PowerPyx and PSNProfiles: 1 platinum, 2 gold, 6 silver, 46 bronze.
Hidden flags: PSNProfiles lists 28 of the 55 as hidden. The 28 flagged here are the story, side-story-finale and cryptic-description trophies; the 27 visible ones are those PSN shows from the start.

trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: Earn the other 54 trophies and this one pops on its own; there is nothing extra to do for it. PowerPyx rates the whole platinum 4/10 and about 200 hours, most of it the 100% checklist, so treat this as the finish line of the roadmap, not a task of its own. No online trophies exist, so the platinum is fully single-player; cheats disable trophies, so keep the whole run cheat-free.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Open Progress > Stats > 100% Completion after the story; the checklist only appears once the credits roll, but everything you did earlier already counts toward it. The checklist is lenient — PowerPyx calls it closer to 60% true completion. You need 70 of the 80 challenges, 200 of 277 base-model vehicles and 100 of 255 animals, while robberies, underwater discoveries, shooting ranges, drone races and Bret's quests need everything. PowerPyx names this the hardest trophy in the game, not because any one task is hard but because it takes about 100 hours after the story.

trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.dispute: Guides split on whether the Chapter 1 balcony session is required. PowerPyx and KeenGamer say do it — it may be the game's only missable. HappyGamer notes only 15 of 18 meditations are needed for 100%, so the balcony may not be required for the trophy either. Our call: do it in Chapter 1; it costs two minutes and removes the risk either way.
trophies.guide: Meditate at every spot across Leonida: 18 meditations across 10 locations — most spots count once per character, so Jason and Lucia each meditate at the same place. DO THIS FIRST: the morning after the Chapter 1 mission Down to Earth, find Lucia in the kitchen at Jason's house. She says she is going to meditate — follow her to the balcony and choose Accept. That session is gone for good once Chapter 1 ends. The other spots stay open for the whole game. Track them under Progress > Collections > Exploration > Meditations, and finish the last one, the Ascent meditation at the peak of Mount Kalaga, only after you can play as both characters (after Coffee Break, Chapter 2). Honest caveat: the balcony session raises the counter by 1 but is not marked as a normal meditation spot, so the guides cannot yet confirm whether the trophy needs it — doing it anyway is the safe play, and 15 of the 18 are what 100% completion asks for.

trophies.guide: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley — bowl a game at that alley. Find the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and play through a game of bowling. Bowling is one of the activity types for Master of None, so this pulls double duty.

trophies.name: Personal Best
trophies.guide: The official description is cryptic: 'A partnership with mass appeal.' It is tied to doing something notable with your partner. Play a partner activity to its best outcome — the trophy is about the two of you, not a solo feat. Exact trigger unconfirmed in the guides we read: which partner moment pops it is not yet pinned down — treat it as a cleanup trophy and check the sources page for updates.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Choices made (for better or worse). PSN tracks a count toward 500 for this trophy. Make choices across the game — dialogue and action choices with your partner and strangers all feed the count. It builds over a full playthrough, so it usually pops during cleanup rather than on its own.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: The official description is cryptic: 'Second time's the charm.' Something in the game needs a second try. Fail a set-piece once and succeed on the second attempt — the trophy is about the retry, not the failure. Exact trigger unconfirmed in the guides we read: which event counts is not yet pinned down — it is a natural-play trophy, so keep playing and it should come.

trophies.name: The Truth Is Out There
trophies.guide: The official description is cryptic: 'What the hell just happened?' Something strange happens somewhere in Leonida. Explore the odd corners of the map — the strange-encounter spots the guides are still mapping — and the moment finds you. Exact trigger unconfirmed in the guides we read: the guides have not pinned down which encounter pops it, so treat it as a late-cleanup trophy.

trophies.name: Ten Pin
trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by — knock someone down with a melee attack from a moving vehicle. Get a vehicle moving, swing a melee weapon as you pass, and knock the target over. A slow drive-by on a quiet street gives you the aim time; the bowling name is a joke, not a bowling alley task.

trophies.name: Dime on the Dollar
trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts. Marked Bills come from robberies — bank vaults, armored trucks and gang operations all pay in them. Launder them through your contacts a little at a time; the total is what counts, not a single wash.

trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all shops. Clothes, weapons, food and car mods all count — normal spending across a full playthrough gets most of the way there. If it has not popped by cleanup, buy out a shop's stock; big-ticket items close the gap fastest.

trophies.name: Little Boxes
trophies.guide: Purchase all garage properties — 8 garages across Leonida. Garages are bought with in-game money, so this is a money trophy in disguise — robberies and laundered bills fund it. Buy each garage as you find it; the trophy pops on the eighth purchase.

trophies.name: On the Spot
trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app. Open the Scooter Bros app and register vehicles you own or find — any 10 count. Register cars as you collect them during the story so this pops early.
